scope: Analytic plane/torus surface-surface intersection in the axial configurations (eighth analytic SS slice, one cell): native intersect_plane_torus in crates/brep-core/src/intersections/plane_torus.rs, bridge op brep_intersect_plane_torus, typed TS adapter intersectPlaneTorus. A new strict canonical ring-torus recognizer (the exact sixteen-patch solid of analytic::torus: 4 profile quadrants x 4 revolution quadrants of rational biquadratic patches, exact tensor-product weights [[1,w,1],[w,w^2,w],[1,w,1]] with w = cos(pi/4) and w^2 computed as the constructor's own product, exact unit-square boundary trims, sixteen ring/quadrant vertices each certified radially and axially against the exact profile, a globally consistent 4x4 quadrant tiling, rigid affine placements admitted) pairs with the canonical planar-patch recognizer of the plane/quadric cells, unchanged. The canonical constructor admits only strict ring tori (R - r >= 1e-5): horn and spindle tori are refused at construction, so the recognizer never certifies a self-intersecting torus. The plane operand is always first — swapped order is an explicit unsupported_surface region. Axial angle classification follows the plane/cylinder discipline: pure-rounding tilts snap (64 binary64 epsilons plus the recognition-error angular allowances), recognition-scale tilts (1e-9) report near_coincidence, clearly oblique planes are unsupported_surface (the general plane/torus section is a quartic with Villarceau degeneracies, out of scope). Perpendicular planes at axial height h resolve empty for |h| > r beyond the outward band, stay tangency_or_multiple_root at |h| == r within the band (never a guessed point or circle), and yield the two exact circles of radii R +- sqrt(r^2 - h^2) otherwise (h == 0 is the equator pair R +- r of the same branch); an inner radius collapsing into the band would be an inner-tangency/horn configuration and stays unresolved (unreachable for a canonical strict ring torus, kept as an honest guard). Through-axis planes (center in the plane at pure-rounding scale) yield the two exact meridian circles of radius r centered at +-R; an axis-parallel plane at a certified nonzero offset cuts a Cassini oval and is unsupported_surface, inside the recognition-scale band near_coincidence. Every circle is clipped by the patch's finite rectangular domain in closed form (eccentric-angle half-plane clip, the plane/sphere cell's clip_ellipse); domain-edge tangencies stay unresolved. Resolved circles are exact rational sweeps (full: four 90-degree arcs, weights cos(pi/4), knots 0..=4) with exact UV lifts on both operands: on the torus the parallels are iso-v lines and the meridians iso-u lines (degree-1 segments, one per covered patch quadrant) whose constant coordinate uses the exact rational 90-degree-arc parameter map t = s/(1+s), s = sqrt(2) tan(phi/2)/(1 - tan(phi/2)) — derived in closed form with discriminant exactly 2, never fitted; on the plane exact rational quadratic ellipse arcs per the recognize_plane metric. Plane/torus coincidence cannot arise (the patches are curved), so coincident_trim is deliberately unused. Nothing here authorizes a topology change.

behaviorChange: New read-only query intersectPlaneTorus (brep_intersect_plane_torus); no existing query, op, or adapter behavior changed. Both dist budgets move once (geometry chunk 2,439,918 to 2,448,493 bytes measured, +8,575 for the ring-torus recognizer, axial classification, exact circle pairs and the iso-parameter lifts — budget now 2,455,000; total 4,758,452 to 4,767,027 bytes measured — budget now 4,775,000)

limits.classificationBand: both recognition deviations + 16 binary64 epsilons of the radius/patch/offset scale
limits.angularSnapBand: 64 binary64 epsilons plus recognition-error angular allowances (pure-rounding tilt only) around the perpendicular and axis-parallel configurations
limits.isoParameterMap: exact rational 90-degree-arc parameter map t = s/(1+s), s = sqrt(2) tan(phi/2)/(1 - tan(phi/2)) (discriminant exactly 2); seam contacts snap at 64 epsilons of the unit parameter interval
limits.conicClip: closed-form eccentric-angle half-plane cuts per patch edge; extrema within the band of a boundary line are tangencies, never clipped through

limitations: Canonical operands only: the planar patch is the one-face open exact bilinear affine rectangle (plane operand first); the torus is the exact canonical strict ring-torus solid (R - r >= 1e-5; horn and spindle tori are refused at construction); everything else is an explicit unsupported_surface region, never a numerical fallback

Axial configurations only: perpendicular planes (parallel circle pair) and through-axis planes (meridian circle pair) are analytic; axis-parallel offset planes cut Cassini ovals and oblique planes cut a quartic with Villarceau degeneracies — both are honest unsupported_surface regions (near-axial bands report near_coincidence), with no numerical fallback

Tangency is never a point or a guessed circle: |h| == r, domain-edge touches and the inner-radius collapse band all stay unresolved, and the classification band widens with recognition deviation so near-tangent configurations below ~1e-13 of the scale stay unresolved rather than guessed
coincident_trim is deliberately unused: a plane can never coincide with a curved torus patch

NumericallyResolved is not certified complete-domain coverage and permitsTopologyChange stays false; consuming these sections in Booleans and the remaining analytic SS pairs (sphere/torus, torus/torus, Villarceau oblique plane/torus, non-parallel cylinder/cylinder) stay open
